pairs.statement: The petition is entered in the register on filing; the registrar writes the case number and the first hearing date on its copies and hands them to the plaintiff for service.
In real-property matters, works on property and leases of property, the claim goes to the court of the place of the property, or of the place where the works are carried out.
The real-property section hears claims to annul, rescind, amend or undo rights arising from published deeds.
Before a claim in which dispute concerns real property is yes and property registered is yes, the petition must be published at the land registry.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not say publication must be completed before bringing the claim. It requires production at the first hearing and provides an exception where deposit for publication is proven.

pairs.statement: A plea of inadmissibility may be raised at any stage of the case, even after a defence on the merits.

A petition concerning a property and/or a real right in property published under the law must be published at the land registry and produced at the first hearing at which the case is called, failing which it is inadmissible in form, unless its deposit for publication is proven.
The code applies to claims before both the ordinary and the administrative courts.
Claims before the real-property section follow this code's procedure, subject to the special provisions on the publication of claims to rescind, annul, amend or undo rights based on published deeds.
Territorial jurisdiction in real-property cases belongs to the court in whose area the property lies, unless the law says otherwise.
Pleas of form must be raised together before any defence on the merits or plea of inadmissibility, failing which they are not accepted.
The appeal petition is entered in the special register subject to the article on fees and on the publication of a real-property petition.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT makes registration subject to Article 17 but does not state that Article 17 concerns fees and publication of real-property petitions.

pairs.statement: An order of protective seizure of real property is entered at the land registry of the property's location within a set period, or the seizure is void; it is a step of the seizure, not of a petition.
The judge raises a plea of inadmissibility of his own motion when it is a matter of public order.
The real-property section hears disputes about immovable property.
The bailiff enters the judgment of adjudication at the land registry for publication within a set period.

Matters the real-property section hears include ownership, other real rights and real securities; possession, prescription, usufruct, use, exploitation and habitation; co-ownership of built property and undivided ownership; partition and boundary-marking; and leases of dwellings and professional premises.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT lists these matters but does not identify the real-property section as the body that hears them.

pairs.statement: The petition mentions, where appropriate, the documents supporting the claim.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT mentions referring to supporting documents where appropriate but does not identify the petition as the document containing that reference.

pairs.statement: The real-property section hears pre-emption cases.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT mentions pre-emption but does not identify the real-property section as the body that hears those cases.
